Re: Customer Appeal—Prior Authorization Denial  
Member: Jordan Brooks  
Member ID: W789350798  
Reference number: POC-E7809C09B9-10970  
Requested service: Total hip replacement  
CPT: 27130  
Denial date: August 3, 2026

Dear Cigna Appeals Reviewer:

I appeal Cigna’s denial of prior authorization for my total hip replacement. The denial states that the submitted records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. The records do document extensive, provider-directed conservative treatment, persistent symptoms, objective structural disease, and substantial functional impairment.

The applicable publicly available Cigna/EviCore policy is CMM-313, Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty, effective March 7, 2026. The policy identifies non-surgical management as including activity modification or relative rest, supervised physical therapy and therapeutic exercises, prescription and non-prescription medications, assistive devices, and intra-articular injections. I have addressed each of these treatment areas as follows:

- I have experienced progressive hip pain for approximately 12 months. Rest has not relieved the pain.
- I used NSAIDs for eight months, with inadequate relief.
- I completed 24 visits of supervised physical therapy over 10 weeks, from May 1, 2026, through July 10, 2026. Therapy focused on hip-abductor strengthening and gait. The physical therapy discharge note documents completion of this course.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on April 20, 2026. It provided only three weeks of partial relief.
- I use a cane because of my symptoms and limited mobility.

The treatment failure is also demonstrated by my continuing disability. I can walk only approximately one block, require a cane, and cannot put on my shoes without assistance. Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.

The objective imaging supports the need for surgery. A weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph dated June 25, 2026, showed superolateral joint-space narrowing to 1 mm, subchondral sclerosis, and osteophytes. These findings are consistent with advanced structural hip disease corresponding to my persistent pain and functional limitations.

There are no documented modifiable issues that would make surgery inappropriate. I have no active infection, no untreated substance-use disorder, a BMI of 29, and I am a nonsmoker. My orthopedic surgeon, Duval, MD, has evaluated me and requested total hip replacement because conservative treatment has not provided durable relief and my symptoms substantially impair daily activities and ambulation.

For these reasons, I request that Cigna overturn the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 27130. If Cigna continues to deny the request, please identify in writing the specific medical-necessity criterion that remains unsatisfied, the records relied upon, and the complete clinical-review criteria applied to this request.

The policy has not been quoted in this letter; the policy discussion above is a plain-language application of the publicly available policy to the clinical records. Please consider the following supporting documents:

1. Physical therapy discharge note documenting 24 visits from May 1, 2026, through July 10, 2026  
2. Medication history documenting eight months of NSAID treatment  
3. Injection record dated April 20, 2026  
4. Weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph report dated June 25, 2026  
5. Orthopedic examination and surgical recommendation from Duval, MD  
6. Prior authorization denial notice dated August 3, 2026

Please acknowledge receipt of this appeal and issue a written determination.

Sincerely,

Jordan Brooks
